raw_response:
The silver step derives txn_date from ingest_ts, which is the delivery time and runs one day after the transaction time. The 2026-01-16 refactor (DE-398) most likely introduced this. The DATE_CONSISTENCY monitor expects txn_date to equal the date of txn_ts.

Evidence that the fix is safe:
- Every sample row has txn_ts one day before ingest_ts.
- All 4558 POSTED rows are flagged, which matches the alert count, so every row is affected.
- txn_ts has no nulls, so the date can be derived directly.

The fix is to set txn_date = CAST(txn_ts AS DATE). The output columns and their types stay the same.

One ambiguity is whether "business date" should be the transaction date or the ingest date. The monitor and the column name txn_date both point to the transaction date, so I treat that as settled.

I did not check for duplicate txn_ids. The profile shows 4827 distinct txn_ids across 4827 rows, so there are none.

Derive txn_date from txn_ts.","decision":"fix","confidence":0.93,"pre_sql":[],"step_overrides":{"silver_transactions":"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
